The '''2017 FA Community Shield''' (also known as '''The FA Community Shield supported by [[McDonald's]]''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 95th [[FA Community Shield]], an annual [[Association football|football]] match played between the winners of the previous season's [[Premier League]] and [[FA Cup]] competitions. It was held at [[Wembley Stadium]] on 6 August 2017. The match was played between [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], champions of the [[2016–17 Premier League]] and [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]], who beat their opponents to win the [[2017 FA Cup final]]. Watched by a crowd of 83,325, Arsenal won the Shield 4–1 on [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalties]], after the match finished 1–1 after 90 minutes. The shoot-out was notable as the [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)#Advantage to team kicking first.3F|ABBA system]] was trialled for the first time in English football; the format sees teams take back-to-back penalties rather than alternating.

[[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]] were the defending champions as winners of the [[2016 FA Community Shield|2016 edition]], but did not qualify for this match, as they finished sixth in the [[2016–17 Premier League|Premier League]] and were knocked out of the [[2016–17 FA Cup|FA Cup]] in the quarter-finals.

This was Arsenal's 22nd Shield appearance to Chelsea's 12th. For Arsenal, [[Alexandre Lacazette]] made his competitive debut, while [[Olivier Giroud]] and [[Theo Walcott]] started as substitutes. Their squad did not include [[Alexis Sánchez]], [[Laurent Koscielny]] and [[Mesut Özil]] – all absent for differing reasons. Midfielder [[Cesc Fàbregas]] started against his former team, playing alongside [[N'Golo Kanté]]. New signings [[Álvaro Morata]], [[Antonio Rüdiger]] and [[Willy Caballero]] were all named on the bench. Striker [[Diego Costa]] was omitted from the Chelsea squad as he did not feature in manager [[Antonio Conte]]'s pre-season preparations.

After a subdued first half, Chelsea took the lead in the 46th minute when [[Victor Moses]] scored. A late challenge by [[Pedro (footballer, born July 1987)|Pedro]] on [[Mohamed Elneny]] resulted in the Chelsea attacker being shown a red card; from the free-kick Arsenal were awarded, substitute [[Sead Kolašinac]] scored on his debut. As there were no further goals, the match was decided by a penalty shoot-out. [[Thibaut Courtois]] and Morata missed their penalties, leaving Giroud to score the winning one.

==Background==
Founded in 1908 as a successor to the [[Sheriff of London Charity Shield]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Abandonment of the Sheriff Shield |page=11 |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=19 April 1908}}</ref> the [[FA Community Shield]] began as a contest between the respective champions of the [[The Football League|Football League]] and [[Southern Football League|Southern League]], although in 1913 it was played between an Amateurs XI and a Professionals XI.<ref>{{cite news |title=The F.A. Charity Shield |page=10 |newspaper=[[The Times]] |location=London |date=7 October 1913}}</ref> In 1921, it was played by the league champions of the top division and [[FA Cup]] winners for the first time.<ref>{{cite news |first=Peter |last=Ferguson |title=The FA Community Shield history |url=http://www.mcfc.co.uk/news/team-news/archive/2011/august/community-shield-2011/the-shield-from-the-beginning |website=mcfc.co.uk |publisher=Manchester City |date=4 August 2011 |access-date=8 August 2014 |archive-date=27 July 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140727202652/http://www.mcfc.co.uk/news/team-news/archive/2011/august/community-shield-2011/the-shield-from-the-beginning |url-status=dead }}</ref>{{#tag:ref|The [[Premier League]] replaced the [[Football League First Division]] at the top of the [[English football league system|English football pyramid]] after its inception in 1992.<ref>{{cite news |title=Continental or the full English? |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2001/dec/02/sport.sportfeatures |first=Alex |last=Fynn |newspaper=The Observer |location=London |date=2 December 2001 |access-date=8 August 2014}}</ref>|group=lower-alpha}} As part of a sponsorship deal between [[The Football Association]] (FA) and American restaurant chain [[McDonald's]], the match was officially referred to as "The FA Community Shield supported by McDonald's".<ref name="Madley"/> It was televised live in the United Kingdom on [[BT Sport|BT Sport 1]],<ref>{{cite news |title=Arsenal v Chelsea: Live stream Community Shield online or watch on TV with BT Sport |url=http://sport.bt.com/football/arsenal-v-chelsea-live-stream-community-shield-online-or-watch-on-tv-with-bt-sport-S11364196591055 |publisher=BT |date=4 August 2017 |access-date=12 August 2017 |archive-date=13 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170813054348/http://sport.bt.com/football/arsenal-v-chelsea-live-stream-community-shield-online-or-watch-on-tv-with-bt-sport-S11364196591055 |url-status=dead }}</ref> with highlights shown later that night on [[BBC One]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Match of the Day, 2017/2018, Community Shield Highlights |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/programmes/b0911y4z |publisher=BBC |access-date=12 August 2017}}</ref> The FA brought forward the kick-off time an hour earlier to avoid a fixture clash with the [[UEFA Women's Euro 2017 final]].<ref>{{cite news |first=Matt |last=Hughes |title=FA moved Arsenal v Chelsea in Community Shield forward for women’s Euro 2017 final |url=https://www.thetimes.com/sport/football/article/fa-moved-arsenal-v-chelsea-in-community-shield-forward-for-womens-euro-2017-final-c5t2bbdmm |newspaper=[[The Times]] |date=1 August 2017 |access-date=12 August 2017}} {{subscription required}}</ref>

[[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] qualified for the 2017 FA Community Shield as winners of the [[2016–17 Premier League]]. The turning point in their season came in September 2016, following successive defeats, first at home to [[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool]] and then away at [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]].<ref name="cont">{{cite news |title=New system changed Chelsea's season, claims Premier League champion Conte |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/news/new-system-changed-chelseas-season-claims-premier-league-champion-conte |magazine=FourFourTwo |date=12 May 2017 |access-date=12 August 2017}}</ref> Manager [[Antonio Conte]] adopted a [[Formation (association football)#3.E2.80.934.E2.80.933|3–4–3]] formation which saw Chelsea embark on a 13-match winning run.<ref name="cont"/> The club won the Premier League with two matches to spare,<ref name="champs">{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Chelsea are Premier League champions: How did Antonio Conte do it? |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39885837 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=12 May 2017 |access-date=12 August 2017}}</ref> and later set a new divisional record for the most wins (30).<ref>{{cite news |title=Are Chelsea champions of the year-on-year football points swing?|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/may/31/are-chelsea-champions-of-the-year-on-year-football-points-swing |website=theguardian.com |date=31 May 2017 |access-date=12 August 2017}}</ref> Chelsea later faced Arsenal in the [[2017 FA Cup final]], on course to complete a [[Double (association football)#England|domestic double]] for the second time in the club's history. A disciplined display by Arsenal, however, saw [[Arsène Wenger]]'s side triumph and secure a Community Shield spot.<ref>{{cite news |first=Phil |last=McNulty |title=Arsenal 2–1 Chelsea |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/39984089 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=27 May 2017 |access-date=12 August 2017}}</ref> Like Conte, Wenger had adopted a similar tactical change during the season, playing three defenders at the back. Arsenal's noteworthy performance in the cup final was attributed to the formation switch.<ref name="cox">{{cite news |first=Michael |last=Cox |title=Arsène Wenger got strategy spot on from back to front in Arsenal win |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/may/28/arsene-wenger-arsenal-chelsea-fa-cup-final-tactics |website=theguardian.com |date=28 May 2017 |access-date=12 August 2017}}</ref>

The 2017 edition was the first competitive fixture in English football to trial the [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)#Advantage to team kicking first.3F|ABBA penalty shoot-out system]], provided scores were level after 90 minutes.<ref name="si">{{cite news |title=Arsenal vs Chelsea Community Shield Will Use 'ABBA' Penalty Shoot-Out System for First Time|url=https://www.si.com/soccer/2017/08/04/arsenal-vs-chelsea-community-shield-will-use-abba-penalty-shoot-out-system-first-time |website=SI.com |date=4 August 2017 |access-date=12 August 2017}}</ref> The format is similar to a [[Tennis scoring system#Scoring a tiebreak game|tiebreak]] in tennis, and is designed "to prevent the team going second from having to play catch-up."<ref>{{cite news |first=Richard |last=Parry |title=Uefa to trial alternative 'ABBA' system for penalty shoot-outs |url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/uefa-to-trial-alternative-abba-system-for-penalty-shootouts-a3530041.html |newspaper=London Evening Standard |date=4 May 2017 |access-date=12 August 2017}}</ref> Unlike a traditional penalty shoot-out, which sees Team A and Team B alternate spot-kicks in an ABAB pattern, the ABBA format follows an 'AB BA AB BA' order.<ref name="si"/>

==Pre-match==
[[File:Arsenal 1 Chelsea 1 (4-1 on pens) (35586041054).jpg|thumb|The Premier League trophy (''left''), the FA Community Shield and the FA Cup displayed on the Wembley Stadium pitch]]

Chelsea were making their twelfth appearance in the Community Shield; prior to this they had won four ([[1970 FA Charity Shield|1970]], [[2000 FA Charity Shield|2000]], [[2005 FA Community Shield|2005]], [[2009 FA Community Shield|2009]]) and lost six, most recently in [[2015 FA Community Shield|2015]] against their present-day opponents.<ref name=rsssf>{{cite web |first=James |last=Ross |title=England – List of FA Charity/Community Shield Matches |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablese/engsupcuphist.html |access-date=1 June 2015 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305035734/http://rsssf.com/tablese/engsupcuphist.html |archive-date=5 March 2016 |website=[[RSSSF]] |df=dmy }}</ref> By contrast, Arsenal made their 22nd Community Shield appearance, and won 13, including one shared in [[1991 FA Charity Shield|1991]]. Both clubs were meeting for the third time in the Shield; their first encounter [[2005 FA Community Shield|12 years ago]] ended 2–1 in Chelsea's favour.<ref name=rsssf/>

Conte used his press conference to reiterate the need for Chelsea to strengthen their squad ahead of the new season: "We have a small squad, I think only one player is not enough to improve our team. We need more players that are not top level like [[Neymar]], but we need to improve our squad."<ref name="mirror">{{cite news |first=Oliver |last=Harbord |title=Antonio Conte full transcript from Chelsea press conference before Community Shield vs Arsenal |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/antonio-conte-full-transcript-chelsea-10931743 |website=Mirror Online |date=4 August 2017 |access-date=12 August 2017}}</ref> He spoke of the importance of winning the fixture as it presented the first trophy of the season and hoped the spectators would see a "good game" against Arsenal.<ref name="mirror"/> Conte ruled [[Eden Hazard]] and [[Tiémoué Bakayoko]] out of the match with injuries and confirmed [[Victor Moses]] would play; the right-wing-back was sent off in the cup final and his one-match suspension carried over to the new season.<ref name="mirror"/> Following a review by the FA in August, Moses was made available for the Community Shield fixture,<ref name="mirror"/> but served a ban against [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]] on the opening weekend of the Premier League season.<ref>{{cite news |first=Ajibade |last=Olusesan |title=Moses out as Chelsea host Burnley |url=https://www.newtelegraphonline.com/2017/08/moses-chelsea-host-burnley/ |newspaper=New Telegraph |location=Lagos |date=12 August 2017 |access-date=12 August 2017 |archive-date=13 August 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170813075459/https://newtelegraphonline.com/2017/08/moses-chelsea-host-burnley/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Wenger told reporters that he saw the Community Shield as "...a good opportunity to repeat the performance from the [FA Cup] final and give competition to players who need it."<ref name="mirr">{{cite news |first=Hamish |last=Mackay |title=Arsenal press conference recap: Arsene Wenger on the Community Shield, Alexis Sanchez and more |url=https://www.mirror.co.uk/sport/football/news/arsenal-press-conference-live-wenger-10921610 |website=Mirror Online |date=3 August 2017 |access-date=12 August 2017}}</ref> When assessing his opponents Chelsea, he noted they had kept the "basis of the squad", and felt Bakayoko was a solid addition.<ref name="mirr"/> The future of [[Alexis Sánchez]] was a major talking point throughout the summer; Wenger adamantly told the press: "My decision is clear, he will stay. He will accept that."<ref name="mirr"/> Midfielder [[Francis Coquelin]] was ruled out by injury, while Sanchez, [[Laurent Koscielny]], [[Aaron Ramsey]] and [[Mesut Özil]] were sidelined.<ref name="mirr"/><ref>{{cite news |first=Seb |last=Stafford-Bloor |title=Community Shield: 5 big talking points from Arsenal 1*-1 Chelsea (4–1 on penalties) |url=https://www.fourfourtwo.com/features/community-shield-5-big-talking-points-arsenal-1-1-chelsea-4-1-penalties |magazine=FourFourTwo |date=6 August 2017 |access-date=12 August 2017 |quote=...even though Arsene Wenger was without the injured Mesut Ozil, Shkodran Mustafi and Aaron Ramsey, as well as the suspended Laurent Koscielny and unfit Alexis Sanchez...}}</ref>

[[Bobby Madley]] was selected as the referee for the Shield match; he had been the [[fourth official]] of the Cup final between the two sides.<ref name="Madley"/> Both clubs received an allocation of approximately 28,300 tickets. Arsenal were housed in the east end of [[Wembley Stadium]], while Chelsea fans occupied the west.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.thefa.com/news/2017/jun/15/fa-competitions-fixture-dates-finals-2017-18-150617 |website=TheFA.com |publisher=The Football Association |title=FA announces competition fixture dates 2017–18 |date=15 June 2017 |access-date=12 August 2017}}</ref> Ticket prices were advertised at a cost of between £20 and £45 – juniors and seniors received concessions of up to £10.<ref>{{cite news |title=Community Shield ticket details announced |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2017/07/community-shield-ticket-details-announced.html |publisher=Chelsea F.C |date=10 July 2017 |access-date=12 August 2017}}</ref> Proceeds from the match went to those affected by the [[Grenfell Tower fire]] in June; families of the victims, survivors, and emergency services personnel were invited to the event as guests.<ref>{{cite news |title=Grenfell Tower fire: Community Shield proceeds to be donated to affected |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40381233 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=23 June 2017 |access-date=12 August 2017}}</ref>

==Match==
===Team selection===
The teamsheets showed both clubs lined-up with a three-man defence.<ref name="teamn">{{cite news |title=Community Shield team news: Arsenal v Chelsea |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2017/08/community-shield-team-news--arsenal-v-chelsea.html |publisher=Chelsea F.C |date=6 August 2017 |access-date=12 August 2017}}</ref> [[Michy Batshuayi]] led the Chelsea attack, either side of [[Pedro (footballer, born July 1987)|Pedro]] and [[Willian (footballer, born 1988)|Willian]].<ref name="teamn"/> Midfielder [[Cesc Fàbregas]] started against his former side, partnering [[N'Golo Kanté]] in midfield, while Moses and [[Marcos Alonso Mendoza|Marcos Alonso]] were deployed as wingbacks.<ref name="teamn"/> Defender [[Gary Cahill]] played his first competitive game as club captain; he officially took over the responsibility from [[John Terry]] in July.<ref>{{cite news |title=Captain Cahill: Delighted, proud and excited |url=http://www.chelseafc.com/news/latest-news/2017/07/captain-cahill--delighted--proud-and-excited.html |publisher=Chelsea F.C |date=26 July 2017 |access-date=12 August 2017}}</ref> Forward [[Alexandre Lacazette]] made his competitive debut for Arsenal, alongside [[Danny Welbeck]] and [[Alex Iwobi]].<ref name="teamn"/> Defender [[Per Mertesacker]],<ref name="cox"/> whose performance against Chelsea in the Cup final earned plaudits, was named in the starting eleven.<ref name="teamn"/> Chelsea's new signings [[Antonio Rüdiger]] and [[Álvaro Morata]] began the game as substitutes, while Arsenal included [[Sead Kolašinac]] and [[Reiss Nelson]] in their matchday squad.<ref name="teamn"/>

===Summary===
[[File:Arsenal 1 Chelsea 1 (4-1 on pens) (36421488725).jpg|thumb|left|[[Per Mertesacker]] was substituted in the first half, having suffered a head injury.]]
The stadium observed a period of silence in memory of the victims of the Grenfell Tower fire; wreaths were laid on the pitch in memory moments before kick-off.<ref name="guardmin">{{cite news |first=Daniel |last=Harris |title=Arsenal 1–1 Chelsea (4–1 on penalties): Community Shield 2017 |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/live/2017/aug/06/arsenal-v-chelsea-community-shield-2017-live |website=theguardian.com |date=6 August 2017 |access-date=17 August 2017}}</ref> Chelsea got the match underway in their home strip of blue, but found their time on the ball limited as Arsenal dictated play.<ref name="guardmin"/> In the seventh minute Iwobi used his pace to get the better of Chelsea defender [[David Luiz]], but his cutback failed to reach Lacazette's feet, instead hitting the striker's body and deflecting wide.<ref name="guardmin"/> Arsenal came forward moments later, when [[Granit Xhaka]]'s pass went over the Chelsea defence and found a roaming Welbeck. The striker's header was easily caught by [[Thibaut Courtois]] in goal.<ref name="bbcmin">{{cite news |first=Gary |last=Rose |title=Community Shield: FT: Arsenal 1–1 Chelsea, Gunners win shootout 4–1 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/live/football/40632496 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=6 August 2017 |access-date=17 August 2017}}</ref> By the midway point of the first half, Chelsea had enjoyed bouts of possession with Pedro and Batshuayi testing their opponents. Arsenal created the first real chance of the game in the 22nd minute; Lacazette spearheaded a counter-attack and his curling shot went around Cahill and against the post.<ref name="bbcmin"/> Lacazette was involved in another move two minutes later, finding [[Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain]] in space, but the England player was intercepted by Moses.<ref name="guardmin"/> Mertesacker required medical attention the 27th minute after colliding with Cahill.<ref name="guardmin"/> The defender was taken off with a head injury and replaced by Kolašinac, who played as left full-back.<ref name="guardmin"/> Chelsea gathered momentum as the half drew to a close; Pedro had a shot saved by Čech, and Willian appealed for a penalty when he fell to the ground in the penalty box after a challenge from [[Héctor Bellerín]].<ref name="guardmin"/><ref name="willian">{{cite news |first=Jack |last=Pitt-Brooke |title=Chelsea manager Antonio Conte vents his anger at referee Bobby Madley after Community Shield defeat to Arsenal |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/chelsea-arsenal-community-shield-antonio-conte-quotes-referee-pedro-sending-off-red-card-bobby-a7879841.html |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220501/https://www.independent.co.uk/sport/football/premier-league/chelsea-arsenal-community-shield-antonio-conte-quotes-referee-pedro-sending-off-red-card-bobby-a7879841.html |archive-date=1 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |newspaper=The Independent |location=London |date=6 August 2017 |access-date=17 August 2017}}{{cbignore}}</ref> The referee, Madley, however booked the midfielder for simulation.<ref name="willian"/>

[[File:Arsenal 1 Chelsea 1 (4-1 on pens) (35586034434).jpg|thumb|[[Thibaut Courtois]] missed his penalty in the shoot-out, sending the ball over the crossbar.]]
In the opening minute of the second half, Chelsea went a goal ahead. A poor clearance by Xhaka from a corner allowed Cahill to head the ball back in the Arsenal box.<ref name="bbcreport">{{cite news |first=Tom |last=Rostance |title=Arsenal 1–1 Chelsea (Arsenal won 4–1 on pens) |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/40766983 |publisher=BBC Sport |date=6 August 2017 |access-date=17 August 2017}}</ref> Moses, rushing in, used his chest to control the ball, before shooting past Čech.<ref name="guardmin"/> Arsenal found it difficult to create clear-cut chances, as Chelsea controlled possession. [[Mohamed Elneny]]’s effort just before the hour mark was well-handled by Courtois, while Welbeck minutes later had his opportunity snuffed out by Luiz.<ref name="guardmin"/> Wenger brought on Giroud and Walcott for Lacazette and Iwobi in the last 30 minutes.<ref name="bbcmin"/> Conte also made an attacking substitution, replacing Batshuayi for Morata.<ref name="bbcmin"/> The turning point of the match came in the 80th minute; a late challenge by Pedro on Elneny resulted in the Chelsea attacker being shown a red card. Arsenal were awarded a free-kick and from that they scored the equaliser.<ref name="bbcreport"/> Xhaka’s delivery met Kolašinac, whose header went across Courtois and into the net.<ref name="bbcreport"/>

No further goals meant the game was decided by a penalty shoot-out. The first three penalties were scored – Cahill for Chelsea, and Walcott and [[Nacho Monreal]] for Arsenal, before Courtois kicked his over the bar and Morata saw his go wide.<ref name="bbcreport"/> Oxlade-Chamberlain converted his and Giroud scored the winning penalty to give Arsenal a 4–1 win in the shoot-out.<ref name="bbcreport"/>

==Post-match==
{{Quote box |width=270px |bgcolor=#c6dbf7 |align=right |quote="The two teams gave everything and the game was of great intensity. Even when we were 1–0 down we didn't panic, kept control of our game and came back." |salign=left |source=—[[Arsène Wenger]] speaking to reporters, post-match.<ref name="skynews">{{cite news |title=Arsene Wenger hails Arsenal form after Community Shield win |url=https://news.sky.com/story/arsene-wenger-hails-arsenal-form-after-community-shield-win-10977414 |publisher=Sky News |date=6 August 2017 |access-date=17 August 2017}}</ref>}}
The result marked the first time Arsenal had won a penalty shoot-out in the Community Shield; they had lost their previous two in [[1993 FA Charity Shield|1993]] and [[2003 FA Community Shield|2003]].<ref name="bbcreport"/> For Chelsea, it was the fourth time in a row they had lost in the Shield.<ref name="bbcreport"/> Conte was puzzled as to why the referee chose to [[Penalty card#Yellow card|book]] Willian, joking had he spoke to Madley "...we would stay and finish the game at 9&nbsp;p.m."<ref name="willian"/> He was disappointed in the manner his team had lost the match, having a man sent off, and called on his players to focus ahead of the new season.<ref name="willian"/> Conte also defended Courtois's spot kick, saying "He is one of the best players [at the club] at taking penalties."<ref>{{cite news |first=Sachin |last=Nakrani |title=Arsène Wenger demands Arsenal build on Community Shield win over Chelsea |url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2017/aug/06/arsenal-chelsea-arsene-wenger-community-shield |publisher=The Guardian |date=6 August 2017 |access-date=17 August 2017}}</ref>

Wenger was heartened by Arsenal's performance, describing the victory as "...an encouragement. Not more than that." He was unsure whether Pedro deserved to be dismissed, but felt his team were growing in the second half and "always looked dangerous."<ref name="bbcreport"/> Of the new season he said, "We have had some bad starts recently in the last four years in the first game of the Premier League. Let's go into the Premier League now with the same discipline and the same spirit and see where we can go."<ref name="skynews"/>

An average of 648,000 viewers watched coverage of the match on BT Sport 1.<ref>{{cite news |first=Stephen |last=Price |title=Wednesday win for Dave |url=http://www.broadcastnow.co.uk/ratings/wednesday-win-for-dave/5120788.article |magazine=Broadcast |location=London |date=11 August 2017 |access-date=17 August 2017}} {{subscription required}}</ref>

The Community Shield marked Wenger's 17th title with Arsenal. However it would turn out to be the final title Arsenal achieved under Wenger as Wenger would leave the club at the end of the [[2017-18 Arsenal F.C. season|2017-18 season]].
